text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock ticked up slightly today, gaining about 0.26%, after falling yesterday as oil prices pulled back on hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East. Over the past two weeks, the stock has climbed nearly 10%, riding a wave of volatility driven by escalating attacks on shipping and oil infrastructure in the Middle East—Houthi militants have targeted Saudi airports and Aramco facilities, while threats from Iran and strikes on Russian oil assets have kept crude prices elevated and refinery margins attractive.

The refining environment remains supportive: U.S. crude sits at $102 and Brent at $126, refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, and fuel inventories are relatively lean, all conditions that typically favor a refiner's profitability. Today's small gain reflects the tug-of-war between geopolitical risk premiums pushing oil higher and periodic optimism about talks that could ease tensions and bring prices down.
